**FAIL — 1 blocking finding, 1 should-fix.** The design aligns with P009 P-5 and BR01/06/07/09. T06 remains unmet because `finish` can seal an unrelated file staged by a security check when the project adopts team measurement during rebase. All **105 focused tests passed**.

### Findings

1. **Blocking · T-4/T-5 · Rebase-time adoption bypasses the early command guard.** In an owned fixture, the project branch began without the team marker and main added it. A declared security check changed and staged `outside.txt`, then exited `0`. `finish` committed the file in `목차 갱신`, rebased onto main, applied the team checks, wrote `TEAM-FINISH.json`, and exited `0`. Merge preview accepted the sealed SHA. The fingerprint is gated on `initialTeamRequired`, while adoption is checked again after the intermediate `git add -A`. A legacy-only control also absorbed the change. Both results reflect the same guard gap. [Early guard](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/harness.ts:1421) · [Intermediate commit](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/harness.ts:1457) · [Final adoption check](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/harness.ts:1480) · [Repro](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/rebase-adoption.py) · [Accepted preview](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/seal-preview.json)
2. **Should-fix · T-5 · The recovery log misclassifies a bookkeeping failure.** A synthetic commit hook refused the bookkeeping commit after FF. The CLI retained one failure event, but labeled it `merge: rebase`. The classifier matches `rebase` in the appended recovery instructions. The actual failure was `git commit`. [Recovery message](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/harness.ts:1621) · [Failure classifier](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/metrics.ts:22) · [Raw log](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/after-ff/repo/projects/P001_261124_synthetic/log.jsonl)

### Acceptance criteria

| Criterion | Result |
|---|---|
| **T-1 · Request measurement** | **Achieved in tested scope.** The current source CLI reported one adopted owner reply and two unconfirmed requests. The wrong-request and out-of-period receipts stayed ignored. The adopted receipt blocked `finish` with exit `2` until explicitly recorded. The legacy projection retained its documented file-presence behavior. |
| **T-2 · Observations and coverage** | **Achieved in tested scope.** The focused suite covered reported values, unknown totals, role attribution, and existing event semantics. |
| **T-3 · Comparisons and baselines** | **Achieved in tested scope.** The focused comparison controls passed. All three named T01 baseline files matched their original Git blobs byte for byte. |
| **T-4 · Retrospective and finish** | **Unmet.** An ignored, untracked `TASK-CLOSE.md` produced a recurring `blocking: 2` finding. `finish` rejected it with exit `2`, preserved HEAD and the source bytes, and passed once the file was explicitly recorded. I found no further material provenance omission or unnecessary refusal in the reviewed collector paths. The rebase-time command guard gap remains blocking. |
| **T-5 · Source CLI and acceptance** | **Unmet.** On projects already using team measurement, the zero-exit security, audit, and ordinary check controls all stopped before committing their staged edits. Equal-ref refusal with no worktree left main clean and the index byte-identical. Restoring the approved ref allowed the retry. Post-FF refusal preserved `병합 대기`, a clean index, and the failure event. The current recovery message calls for a fresh preview SHA and stopping to preserve both logs on conflict. The focused Korean-path control passed with the default Git adapter and NUL-delimited tree names. |

Current source paths and evidence for the provenance and merge controls are available in [input selection](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/team-metrics.ts:83), [index comparison](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/team-finish.ts:41), [NUL tree lookup](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/team-finish.ts:59), [FF tracking](/Volumes/Data/AiStudio/workspace/pace.wt/P009/src/project/harness.ts:1599), and [case results](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/case-results.json).

### Evidence and limits

- Ran `node --test test/team-metrics.test.ts test/team.test.ts` once on Node `v24.22.3`. **105 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped.** Made **41 additional source CLI calls** in owned synthetic repositories and PACE_HOME directories. The first answer fixture included `closed` in a receipt period and was rejected. I retained that transcript, corrected the receipt shape, and anchored the measurement window to the fixture’s start event. No product edits, installation, real merges, transmission, or process termination occurred. The full suite remains with the PM. [Focused log](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/focused.log) · [Raw commands](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/commands.jsonl) · [Initial fixture](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/probe.log) · [Corrected fixture](/tmp/pace-t06-independent-r8.sjfgzZ/probe-corrected.py)
- Fresh independent Codex tester, same OpenAI provider, `cross=false`. I read the prior judgments and the TASK, PROJECT, and four briefs. Stage18’s SHA matrix, basic ignored-proof and legacy collision controls, and manual recovery retry remain historical evidence. I used no PM disposition or CLOSE as success evidence. The 36-file target patch passed reverse-apply checks before and after, with SHA-256 `0d2ad892e3ca8e4f00041782649760c4bb4ac97b15f6cb9b17384b9c92d141e4`.
- `owner` denotes the existing `user` actor. Captain protocol compatibility is outside the agreed contract. `--no-launch` records `runtimeObserved:false`. Generic definition-change receipts still leave their meaning to human review, and metadata and SHAs provide no human authentication. The documented whole-document lone-CR limitation remains. T06 and T07 obligations remain in force. Actual adoption, efficacy, and live retrospective use are **unknown**, held for T08 after main merge and installation.
